Hi Irene,

Attached are ACME's proposed redlines to the pricing exhibit for the order form (see ACME_redline_pricing_schedule_2028-04-24.docx and summary). High-level asks:

- Add a hard "cap" on per-month spend for the first 12 months tied to a monthly usage ceiling;
- Insert a minimum spend "floor" on a per-quarter basis but with a 90-day true-up window;
- Add a contractual discount floor for model variants (we've requested a 35% minimum discount for quantized variants);
- Clarify packaging: separate line items for hosted API versus dedicated capacity and an explicit ramp schedule.

We appreciate Redwood's flexibility but legal needs the redline so procurement can sign off. Do you have any concerns with the proposed language, or will Redwood need to offer alternate wording for caps/floors? If possible, we'd like a short call Thursday to reconcile.

Hi Maya — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. I pulled the attachments into our queue and looped in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Sales) to get alignment. Quick read: we understand the ask on caps/floors but there are a few points we can't accept verbatim.

A few initial notes:
- Hard monthly "cap" language as written could conflict with our autoscaling cost model. We can offer an "annualized commit cap" tied to a billing true-up and a short burst carveout.
- The 90-day floor true-up is workable if the floor is expressed as an annualized minimum with quarterly measurement windows — otherwise it creates billing churn that will materially increase unit prices.
- Discount floor for quantized variants: we typically provide model-specific discounts but need to limit guaranteed minimums per-model. We can propose a graduated discount table by model family instead of a blanket 35% floor.

Laura — can you review the attached redline and propose language that: (1) preserves ACME's risk protection; (2) preserves Redwood's ability to autoscale under burst traffic; and (3) narrows the scope of guaranteed discounts to product families?

Maya — would you be open to a 30-minute call Thursday PST to walk through one consolidated redline? If so, propose a time and we'll confirm.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 Apr 2028 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME pricing exhibit — legal commentary

Internal notes for Irene and Karthik (do not forward without redline tracked changes):

I've reviewed ACME's redline. Key legal recommendations and suggested replacement language follow — I've also attached a short commentary file.

1) Replace "hard cap on per-month spend" with: "Annualized Commit Cap" — defined as the maximum committed spend for the 12-month term, subject to pro rata adjustments for partial terms and an express burst allowance of up to 10% of the average monthly commit for unplanned traffic. This avoids ambiguity with autoscale billing.

2) For the "floor" language, propose: Quarterly Measurement with 60-day True-Up. Floor should be calculated on an annualized basis and measured quarterly to reduce short-term volatility. The true-up mechanism should allow either payment for shortfalls or credit application, at Redwood's election.

3) Discount floors for quantized variants — recommend rejecting a flat guaranteed percentage. Instead: include a Discount Schedule (by product family) with guaranteed range bands (e.g., 15-30% for quantized family A, 25-40% for quantized family B), and include a migration clause to allow Redwood to change recommended discounts with 60 days notice tied to measurable model improvements.

4) Packaging/line items: Suggest separate SOW appendix listing SKU definitions and a ramp schedule (months 1-3: onboarding credits; months 4-12: committed ramp tiers). This keeps the order form clean and lets ops reconcile line-level usage.

If these are acceptable in principle, I can prepare a tracked-changes version of the pricing exhibit that implements these edits (target EOD tomorrow).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit redlines for upcoming order form — Acme Health

Maya — thanks for the patience. We reviewed ACME's redlines and Laura drafted alternate language that we think preserves the protections you're asking for while addressing our operational constraints. High-level proposed compromise (see attached legal_commentary_ACME_pricing_2028-04-27.txt for full wording):

- Annualized Commit Cap: we propose an "Annualized Commit Cap" definition rather than a hard per-month cap. This commits an annual spend that is measured monthly for billing and allows a 10% burst allowance for traffic spikes outside of scheduled usage.
- Floor True-Up: switch to quarterly measurement with a 60-day true-up window. To reduce churn, true-ups can be satisfied by invoice payment or applied credits at Redwood's option.
- Discount Schedule: we'll include a model-family Discount Schedule in an appendix with guaranteed discount bands rather than a flat 35% cross-model floor. This allows predictable pricing while keeping discounts aligned to model improvements.
- Packaging: we'll create a short Appendix A that enumerates SKUs for Hosted API vs Dedicated and a 4-month ramp schedule with onboarding credits, so invoicing maps cleanly to usage.

Next steps:
1) If ACME can accept the high-level compromise, we'll produce a tracked-changes pricing exhibit reflecting the edits and send for your review.
2) If you're comfortable, we'll include a proposed DocuSign packet (Order Form + Appendix A + Discount Schedule) for signature once everybody signs off.

Proposed times for a short call to finalize language: Thu 03 May 09:00 PT or Fri 04 May 11:00 PT — let me know which works.

If you prefer, I've pasted the core compromise bullet text below for quick copy/paste into your internal review.

— Irene
